newsitem.title: UK: U.S. 1996 chemical trade surplus seen at $17bln.
newsitem.headline: U.S. 1996 chemical trade surplus seen at $17bln.

text.p: - The U.S. chemical industry is expected to report a trade surplus of around $16.9 billion for last year, down from $20.4 billion in 1995, the president of the U.S. Chemical Manufacturers' Association Fred Webbber said on Thursday.

Speaking to a business outlook conference at Britain's Chemical Industries Association, Webber said that exports from the U.S. rose only around 1.4 percent last year while imports rose by 11.1 percent.
Webber said that based on 10 months' data the association expects total exports of $61.8 billion in 1996 and imports of around $44.9 billion.
Chemicals are the U.S.'s biggest export sector, accounting for more than 10 percent of U.S. exported goods.
Webber said spending on research and development by the industry is expected to have risen by around 4.0 percent to $18.3 billion last year.

And based on figures for the first three quarters of 1996, Webber predicted record profits for the industry including pharmaceuticals of at least $43 billion "even if the fourth quarter performance lags significantly."
Profits in industrial chemicals are expected to total around $11.8 billion for the full year, beating the 1995 record of $11.0 billion.
